title: FPV Drone
description: An FPV drone shot is first-person aerial flying: the camera banks, dives, and threads architecture at high speed. It is proximity and flight, a racing craft with a lens, not a slow crane and not a high establishing hover.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: Impossible closeness at velocity. Windows, girders, and shoulders are obstacles in a flight path, not composition toys at a distance.
The horizon rolls because the craft banks. It is the wrong tool for a chapter-close aerial pullback, and the wrong tool for a dialogue two-shot.
If the drone flies like a tripod, you wanted a different aerial.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: A small quad flown in first-person view, often with a bound or slightly stabilized camera. Banked turns, fast acceleration, edge motion blur, proximity to surfaces.
Name the route and the end composition. Prompt FPV drone racing past the subject, first-person flight, banking turns, proximity to architecture, motion blur on edges.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it for impossible proximity and speed. Concrete beat: through a hangar, past a fuselage, out a door, into sky.
Do not FPV a still interview.

sections.title: Compared with similar shots

blocks.text: An Aerial Pullback rises and recedes until geography wins, usually from helicopter or high drone with a level horizon. A Crash Zoom In is an optical snap from sticks, not a fly-by.
A Crane Up is an arm on the ground, tens of feet, not a missile path. FPV is 6DOF flight.
Aerial PullbackClose a chapter. Geography wins.

sections.title: In film

blocks.text: Top Gun: Maverick second-unit language made high-speed proximity a feature grammar. Music-video FPV popularized threading architecture and bodies at racing speeds.
Use the banked path and the near-miss, not a particular jet.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is a slow Aerial Pullback or a Crane Up. The tell is a level, hovering horizon and no bank.
The fix: first-person flight, banking, speed, named obstacles, a physical end frame.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is FPV Drone in film?
It is a first-person-view drone path that banks and threads space at speed, with the camera flying as a small aircraft rather than hovering as a crane.
FPV Drone vs Aerial Pullback
Aerial pullback recedes until a person is a mark on a map, usually level and high. FPV stays close, banks, and treats architecture as a course.
When should I use FPV Drone?
When proximity and speed are the information. Do not use it to gently reveal a landscape.
How do I prompt FPV Drone for AI image or video?
Write FPV drone, first-person flight, banking turns, proximity to structures, edge blur, named route and end composition. Ban a slow level crane.
